History 2011-II.question: In 1856, Awadh would not have been annexed with the British empire if the Nawab of Awadh had

not refused to introduce reforms as suggested by the British
fought against the British

History 2011-II.explanation: (b)  Lord Dalhousie was keen on annexing the kingdom of Awadh. But the task presented certain difficulties because the Nawab of Awadh had been a British ally since the Battle of Buxar and had been most obedient to the British over the years. Lord Dalhousie hit upon the idea of alleviating the plight of the people of Awadh and accusing Nawab Wajid Ali on the ground of misgovernance and annexed his state in 1856. 111. (d) Doctrine of lapse, in Indian history, formula devised by Lord Dalhousie, governor-general of India (1848-56), to deal with questions of succession to Hindu Indian states. According to 'Doctrine of Lapse', if any ruler of a protected state died without a natural heir, the states' authority will pass to the English East India Company. Annexation in the absence of a natural or adopted heir was enforced in the cases of Satara (1848), Jaitpur and Sambalpur (1849), Baghat (1850), Chota Udaipur (1852), Jhansi (1853), and Nagpur (1854).

It made the annexation of Indian State compulsory after the death of a ruler

History 2011-II.subject: History
History 2011-II.question: Which one among the following was not a possible reason for the success of Nadir Shah’s military compaign in Delhi?
options: Weak Mughal emperor
Lack of strong defence in the North-West frontier
Late preparation for the defence of Delhi
Use of superior military technology by the invading army
History 2011-II.answer: Use of superior military technology by the invading army
History 2011-II.explanation: (d)  Nadir Shah, was the founder of the Afsharid dynasty. Nadir Shah led his army which consisted of 80,000 armymen. He placed 3,000 of his army men in the front as a clear line of defence against the Mughal army. Nadir Shah advanced towards India in 1738. At the battle of Karnal on 13 February 1739, Muhammad Shah was defeated and surrendered. The whole city of Delhi was destroyed, looted, plundered and ruined by the army of Nadir Shah. Nadir Shah took with him the Peacock throne built by Shah Jahan. He also took the legendary "Koh-i- noor" diamond.

History 2011-II.subject: History
History 2011-II.question: What was the ‘privy purse’ in the context of the history of modern India?

A purse given by the Government of India to dignitaries for services rendered

History 2011-II.subject: History
History 2011-II.question: The Jainas believe the Jainism is the outcome of the teachings of 24 tirthankaras. In the light of this statement, which one among the following is correct of Vardhamana Mahavira?
options: He was the first tirthankara and the founder of Jainism
He was the 23rd tirthankara, the first 22 tirthankaras being considered legendary
He was the last and 24th tirthankara, who was not considered as the founder of the new faith but as a reformer of the existing religious sect
He was not one of the 24 tirthankaras
History 2011-II.answer: He was the last and 24th tirthankara, who was not considered as the founder of the new faith but as a reformer of the existing religious sect
History 2011-II.explanation: (c)  Mahavira was a teacher of the religion of Jainism. He lived in India. His followers believed that he was the 24th in a line of great teachers. These teachers were called tirthankaras.

History 2011-II.subject: History
History 2011-II.question: Which one among the following statements appropriately defines the term ‘Drain Theory’ as propounded by Dadabhai Naoroji in his work ‘Poverty and Un–British Rule in India’?
options: That a part of India’s national wealth or total annual product was being exported to Britain for which India got no material returns
That the resources of India were being utilised in the interest of Britain
That the British industrialists were being given a opportunity to invest in India under the protection of the imperial power
That the British goods were being imported to India making the country poorer day by day
History 2011-II.answer: That a part of India’s national wealth or total annual product was being exported to Britain for which India got no material returns
History 2011-II.explanation: (a)  Dadabhai Naoroji was the first man to say that internal factors were not the reasons of poverty in India but poverty was caused by the colonial rule that was draining the wealth and prosperity of India. In 1867, Dadabhai Naoroji put forward the 'drain of wealth' theory in which he stated that the Britain was completely draining India. He mentioned this theory in his book Poverty and Un- British Rule in India.
